title: Auditing Agentic SAE Explainers for Confident Hallucination

original_idea.body:
# Auditing Agentic SAE Explainers for Confident Hallucination

**Problem:** Agentic explainer frameworks use an LLM to interpret SAE features; if it confidently mislabels a safety feature, downstream monitoring inherits a hidden error.

**Direction:** Run an open LLM as an SAE-feature explainer over public features including safety-relevant ones, verify against activating examples, measure confident-wrong rate and whether errors cluster on abstract/safety features.

**Why it matters:** Unaudited explainers are a single point of failure for interpretability-based safety.

**Relevant context:** arXiv 2511.20820; arXiv 2507.08473; Neuronpedia.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (explainer errors corrupt monitoring) but a step from any deployed safety guarantee.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Run an LLM explainer over public features + verify against activating examples; guided.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Pure inference on public artifacts, audit labs won't prioritize; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: LLM inference over public features; single mid GPU (or API).

novelty.reasoning: Agentic explainers are new; an explicit hallucination audit on safety features may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Explainer frameworks are new; the safety-feature hallucination audit may be open.
